label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, pool-exhaustion, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 8 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT cents (unchanged), REFUND_CONNECTION kept -> returned); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: pool-exhaustion
case.title: Payments fail: the payments API's database pool runs dry
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the payments API with a connection leak (REFUND_CONNECTION=kept): reading a payment's refunds takes a connection from its database pool of 10 and never gives it back, so after about ten refunds the pool is empty, and every request waits for a connection until the pool's 5 s timeout, then fails with a 500.
case.remedy: roll the payments API back to REFUND_CONNECTION=returned: its new container starts with a full pool

expected_symptoms: the pool runs dry about 40 to 50 s after the deploy; then POST /payments takes 5 to 8 s (a worker thread, then the pool's 5 s wait) and fails with a 500: the p95 latency passes 7 s, and the 5xx share passes 70% within a minute
the payments API logs 'unhandled error' with PoolTimeout: no connection within 5 s
its health check fails too, so docker marks it unhealthy, while PostgreSQL itself is up
the traffic's clients retry and give up: many payments end with their outcome unknown, and arrivals past 64 in flight are shed
the money check passes: a payment that never got a connection was never charged, and one charged before its answer was lost is confirmed by its webhook
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to REFUND_CONNECTION=returned: its new container starts with a full pool

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 17:31:10 with REFUND_CONNECTION=kept. That setting most likely makes each refund request keep its Postgres connection instead of returning it to the psycopg pool. Refunds ran at about 0.25–0.36/s, so a small pool would drain in roughly 30 s. From about 17:31:40, every POST /payments waits the full 5 s pool timeout for a connection, then fails with psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout and HTTP 500. Those fixed ~5.01 s waits are what push p95 to 7.3 s. The provider is not the cause: its calls stay under 10 ms. Open questions: I could not see the settings before this deploy, so I cannot prove REFUND_CONNECTION was the setting that changed. I also did not see a direct count of pool connections held by the refund path. The link from refunds to the leak is inferred from timing, the setting's name and the PoolTimeout errors.

evidence.shows: p95 of payments-api server requests was ~0.02 s until 17:31, then 7.33 s at 17:32:02, confirming the alert.
payments-api was the only service redeployed just before the spike (17:31:10), with settings REFUND_CONNECTION=kept, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents.
payments-api calls to the provider stay fast (p95 ≤ 10 ms), so the latency is not at the provider.
Slow POST /payments requests from 17:31:27 onward all take ~5.01 s, which looks like a fixed timeout.
One slow request spends ~5 s waiting between two Redis calls with no Postgres span, then fails with error.type psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout and HTTP 500.
payments-api logs show a steady stream of PoolTimeout errors on POST /payments.
Refunds were succeeding at ~0.3/s. 500s on /payments start at 17:31:40, about 30 s after the deploy, and climb to 4.8/s while 201s fall. Refunds start failing with 500s too.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings from before the 17:31:10 deploy, which should restore refunds returning their connections to the pool. Recreating the container also frees the connections held now. Then confirm that p95 drops and PoolTimeout errors stop, and run money_check, because refunds and payments that failed mid-flight may have left state that disagrees with the provider.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail briefly; clients may retry, and idempotency keys in Redis cover those retries. The rollback also reverts the deploy's other settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT) to whatever they were before. If one of those changed too, its old behavior returns. That matters most for CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT, since a wrong amount unit would misprice charges.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If things get worse, redeploy payments-api with the current settings (REFUND_CONNECTION=kept, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents). Before doing so, look at the deploy log to see exactly which setting the rollback changed.
